units.title: Queries, keys, values and scaled dot-product attention
outcomes: Derive the 1/sqrt(d_k) scale from unit-variance query and key components and state the assumption it needs.
Implement stable scaled dot-product attention from tensor operations, with a row-wise softmax that cannot overflow in fp32.
Explain attention output as a convex combination of values and predict how a logit shift moves the weights.
units.why: Attention is the only communication path between positions in a transformer. If the scale, the softmax axis or the stability fix is wrong, every later block inherits the error.

next.note: Feed masked scores into the same row-wise softmax.
Reuse single-head attention inside per-head projections.

study.title: Equivalent-implementation box
study.locator: The Efficient implementation equivalent code box: default scale 1/sqrt(E), score-times-scale order, and softmax-then-dropout order

focus: Queries, keys and values are three learned linear maps of the same input. D2L builds them bias-free by default while UDL equations 12.4 and 12.6 carry bias vectors, so the two parameter counts differ by construction.

Under independent zero-mean unit-variance components, q^T k has variance d. The 1/sqrt(d) factor restores unit variance before the softmax; without it large d saturates the softmax and gradients vanish.
Stable softmax subtracts the row max first. Naive fp32 softmax on logits such as UDL Problem 12.4 overflows to NaN, while the shifted form returns the correct weights.

UDL lays inputs out as D by N columns with softmax per column; D2L uses batch by queries by keys with softmax on the last axis. In both, exactly one axis sums to 1: check which one before reading any heatmap.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, derive the 1/sqrt(d) scale from the variance argument. Then hand-compute the Deep-ML 490 first test: scores [[0.7071, 0], [0, 0.7071]], weights [[0.6698, 0.3302], [0.3302, 0.6698]], output [[1.6605, 2.6605], [2.3395, 3.3395]].
traps: Computing softmax as exp(z)/sum(exp(z)) in fp32. exp(100) overflows to inf and the row becomes NaN; always subtract the row max, and recheck any code that skips it.
Softmaxing the wrong axis after a transpose. UDL and D2L sum over different axes by layout; a heatmap that sums to 1 along queries instead of keys inverts the routing story.
Quoting D2L parameter counts for UDL equations or vice versa. The bias terms add 3D parameters; carry them only when the equations you implement include them.

selfTest.q: Query and key components are independent with zero mean and unit variance, in dimension d. What are the mean and variance of their dot product, and what scale restores unit variance?
selfTest.a: Mean 0 and variance d, since the dot product sums d independent unit-variance products. Multiply by 1/sqrt(d) to restore unit variance before the softmax.

selfTest.q: Naive fp32 softmax meets UDL Problem 12.4 logits [-3, 1, 100, 5, -1]. What comes out, what does the max-subtracted form give, and what do the 25 derivatives say?
selfTest.a: Naive exp overflows at exp(100), giving inf and a NaN row. Max-subtracted softmax gives y3 near 1 and the rest near 0. All 25 derivatives are near 0 (largest magnitude about 5.5e-42): a saturated softmax with vanishing gradients.

selfTest.q: A self-attention block takes N = 5 inputs of width D = 8, with queries, keys and values also width 8. How many QKV weights and biases, how many attention weights, and how many weights and biases in a fully connected DN to DN map?
selfTest.a: QKV: 3 times (64 + 8) = 216. Attention weights: 25. Fully connected: 1600 weights plus 40 biases = 1640.

selfTest.q: Why must attention weights be nonnegative and sum to one, and where does each output lie?
selfTest.a: They form a convex combination, so each output is a weighted average of the value vectors and lies in their convex hull. Routing language only makes sense under this constraint.

study.title: Mask semantics, causality and dropout
study.locator: The boolean-mask Note (True means participate, inverse of MultiheadAttention key_padding_mask), the is_causal parameter entry including the non-square upper-left bias, and the dropout Warning that dropout applies in every mode

focus: Padding and causal masks compose by intersection: a score survives only if both allow it. D2L valid_lens expresses padding lengths, the decoder [1..n] rows express causality, and a real batch needs both at once.
Mask value conventions differ by API. SDPA bool True means participate while MultiheadAttention key_padding_mask True means mask out. Copying one convention into the other leaks padding.

A fully masked row has no agreed meaning. D2L -1e6 gives uniform weights, all -inf through plain softmax gives NaN, and SDPA on CPU returned zeros in version 2.14. Test your convention instead of assuming one.
SDPA applies dropout_p in every mode. Pass 0.0 outside training or evaluation outputs stay stochastic.
units.reproduce: From a blank file, build combined causal plus padding masks for two sequences of valid lengths 3 and 2 over 4 keys, show every disallowed weight is exactly 0, then change a future token and a padded value and show the earlier valid outputs do not move.
traps: Trusting uniform weights on a fully masked row. D2L returns 1/n there, so padding values still mix into the output unless you zero the row downstream.
Passing both attn_mask and is_causal to SDPA. The function raises an error; pick one expression of the same mask.
Leaving dropout_p nonzero during evaluation or testing. Outputs differ run to run and differential tests against a manual path fail for no structural reason.

selfTest.q: D2L masked_softmax meets a row with valid length 0 over 4 keys. What weights come out and why is that dangerous?
selfTest.a: Uniform weights 0.25 each: all four -1e6 entries softmax equally. The output mixes padding values with full weight, so the row must be zeroed or excluded downstream.

selfTest.q: An SDPA bool mask marks padding as True. What happens, and how does MultiheadAttention key_padding_mask differ?
selfTest.a: SDPA treats True as participate, so padding joins attention: a leak. MultiheadAttention key_padding_mask uses the inverse convention, True means mask out. Invert when migrating.

selfTest.q: Why is a future-token intervention a stronger causal proof than reading attention weights?
selfTest.a: Weights show one layer; dropout, residuals and later layers remix paths. Perturbing a future token and requiring earlier outputs to stay fixed tests the composed block, including leaks through paths the weight plot never shows.

selfTest.q: SDPA is called with dropout_p 0.5 during evaluation. What goes wrong?
selfTest.a: Dropout still applies in every mode, so outputs stay stochastic. Pass 0.0 when the caller is not training.

study.title: Decoder self versus encoder-decoder attention
study.locator: TransformerDecoderBlock: attention1 over (X, key_values, key_values) with dec_valid_lens versus attention2 over (Y, enc_outputs, enc_outputs) with enc_valid_lens

focus: D2L sets per-head width to num_hiddens over num_heads, so all four projections stay num_hiddens by num_hiddens. The head count changes mixing, not size.

Heads fold into the batch axis: (batch, steps, heads, width) becomes (batch times heads, steps, width) for the shared attention call, then unfolds back. valid_lens must repeat once per head to stay aligned.
Cross-attention reuses the identical math with different sources: queries from the decoder state, keys and values from encoder outputs, with padding-only lengths.
UDL Problem 12.5 is the cost intuition: narrow heads at fixed total width keep the implementation efficient.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, walk shapes for batch 2, 4 queries, width 100, 5 heads: projections stay (2, 4, 100), folded per-head tensors are (10, 4, 20), concatenation restores (2, 4, 100). State BERT per-head width 64 from 1024 over 16 heads.
traps: Reshaping before transposing in the head split. Splitting num_hiddens into heads and head width must precede the sequence-axis move, or head and position entries interleave.
Forgetting the valid_lens repeat after folding. The folded batch has batch times heads rows; unrepeated lengths mask the wrong rows.
Assuming cross-attention needs a new formula. Only the sources change; calling self-attention with (Y, encoder outputs, encoder outputs) is the whole difference.

selfTest.q: BERT uses width 1024 with 16 heads. What is the per-head width, and what shape are its per-head query matrices?
selfTest.a: 64. Each per-head query, key and value matrix is 64 by 1024.

selfTest.q: Why does fixing total width while varying head count hold parameters and compute flat?
selfTest.a: All four projections stay num_hiddens by num_hiddens regardless of head count, so QKVO parameters stay 4 times width squared and per-head matmuls sum back to the same total.

selfTest.q: In the D2L decoder block, which tensors supply queries, keys and values to the second attention call, and which lengths mask it?
selfTest.a: Queries come from the decoder state Y after self-attention; keys and values come from encoder outputs. Only encoder padding lengths mask it; there is no causal mask on this call.

selfTest.q: The valid_lens repeat per head is deleted. What breaks?
selfTest.a: The folded batch has batch times heads rows but only batch lengths. Rows past the batch index read out of range or reuse row zero lengths, so heads mask the wrong key slots.

study.title: Positional encoding implementation and theory
study.locator: Positional Encoding: the sine-cosine formula, the PositionalEncoding class with max_len 1000 and dropout after the add, the encoding_dim 32 with num_steps 60 run plotting columns 6:10, the binary-frequency intuition, and the relative-offset rotation derivation

study.title: Order-free self-attention
study.locator: The paragraphs before Positional Encoding on parallel computation discarding sequential order

focus: Without positions the block is permutation-equivariant: Sa[XP] equals Sa[X]P. UDL Problem 12.3 asks for this proof; it is the reason order must be injected as input.
Absolute encodings add a unique column per position. D2L scales embeddings by sqrt(width) first because raw encodings live in [-1, 1].
Sinusoid pairs rotate with offset: position i plus delta is a fixed 2x2 rotation of position i, depending on delta and frequency only. Shifting text shifts encodings linearly.
Relative schemes index by the offset between key and query positions, not by absolute index. They survive absolute shifts that absolute tables must relearn.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, write p(i, 2j) and p(i, 2j+1), sketch the Sa[XP] equals Sa[X]P proof, and verify the 2x2 rotation numerically for one (i, delta, j) triple.
traps: Adding positions to queries and keys but not values, or the reverse, without noticing. UDL flags both placements; each changes what downstream layers can read about order.
Exceeding D2L max_len 1000. The stored table is fixed width, so longer inputs fail on the add; rebuild the table instead of truncating silently.
Treating dropout placement as free. D2L drops out after adding encodings, so train and eval runs see different position noise; compare runs in eval mode.

selfTest.q: State permutation equivariance for self-attention and explain why it forces positional input.
selfTest.a: Sa[XP] equals Sa[X]P for any permutation matrix P: reordering inputs reorders outputs identically. The block therefore carries no order information, so positions must enter as extra input.

selfTest.q: Write the D2L sinusoidal encoding entries.
selfTest.a: p(i, 2j) equals sin(i / 10000^(2j/d)) and p(i, 2j+1) equals cos(i / 10000^(2j/d)), with i the position and d the width.

selfTest.q: What does the 2x2 rotation from position i to position i plus delta depend on?
selfTest.a: Only the offset delta and the pair frequency omega_j. It never depends on the absolute position i, which is why a fixed shift is a fixed linear map.

selfTest.q: A 1500-token input meets D2L default PositionalEncoding. What happens?
selfTest.a: The stored table is 1000 wide, so the slice caps at 1000 and the add fails on shape mismatch. Rebuild the encoding with a larger max_len.
